full_text_en:
Fang Zebo v. Huilai County Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China — Dispute over Simplified Personal Insurance Benefits

Plaintiff: Fang Zebo, male, 24 years old, teacher at Donglong Middle School, Huilai County, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Huilai County Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China.

Legal Representative: Lin Shuijiang, Manager.

Agent ad litem: Xie Weimin, Deputy Section Chief of the Personal Insurance Division, Huilai County Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China.

Agent ad litem: Huang Liefeng, Lawyer, Huilai County Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Fang Zebo, filed a lawsuit against the defendant, Huilai County Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China, concerning its refusal to pay the simplified personal insurance benefits for his father. The case was brought to the Huilai County People's Court of Guangdong Province. After a public trial, the court found the following facts:

The plaintiff's father, Fang Fengrong, was an employee of the Huilai County Food Company during his lifetime. On May 12, 1985, Fang Fengrong was hospitalized due to illness and was diagnosed with bladder cancer. After undergoing a partial cystectomy and left ureteral transplant surgery, he was discharged and returned to work. In August 1986, the Huilai County Food Company mobilized its employees to participate in simplified personal insurance and explained the insurance conditions. Subsequently, the company contributed RMB 2 per month for each employee, and Fang Fengrong contributed RMB 3 per month, voluntarily purchasing 5 units of simplified personal insurance with an insurance period of 15 years. The policy provided that if the insured survived until the maturity date or died due to illness or accidental injury during the effective insurance period, the insurance company would pay insurance benefits of RMB 1,140. The policy explicitly stated that persons suffering from cancer and other diseases were not eligible to apply for insurance. The insurance company issued Fang Fengrong a simplified personal insurance certificate. On May 8, 1987, Fang Fengrong was hospitalized for emergency treatment and was diagnosed with upper gastrointestinal bleeding — compound ulcer, postoperative metastasis of bladder cancer, urinary tract infection, and systemic failure. He died on August 19 of the same year. Thereafter, the plaintiff applied to the defendant for insurance benefits based on the insurance certificate. The defendant refused to pay the benefits, claiming that Fang Fengrong had concealed the insurance conditions by applying for insurance while ill, which fell outside the scope of insurance coverage, and only refunded the insurance premiums. The plaintiff disagreed and filed a lawsuit with the court.

The above facts are confirmed by hospital diagnosis certificates, documentary evidence from the insurance company and the Food Company, and the evidence is sufficient and conclusive.

The Huilai County People's Court held that although the plaintiff's father, Fang Fengrong, had suffered from bladder cancer before applying for insurance, he was able to return to work after surgery. The conclusion of the Huilai County Hospital regarding Fang Fengrong's cause of death was not solely due to metastasis of bladder cancer. Therefore, the defendant's claim that the insurance contract was invalid on the grounds that Fang Fengrong concealed the insurance conditions at the time of application was improper. Pursuant to Articles 85 and 84(2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, a contract lawfully formed is protected by law. A creditor has the right to demand that the debtor perform its obligations in accordance with the terms of the contract. According to Article 5(1)(2) of the Simplified Personal Insurance Clauses (Type A), which provides that "if the insured dies due to illness or accidental injury during the effective insurance period, the full amount of insurance benefits shall be paid," the defendant should pay the plaintiff the full amount of insurance benefits. Accordingly, on June 13, 1989, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The simplified personal insurance contract entered into between Fang Fengrong and the defendant, Huilai County Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China, is valid.

2. The defendant shall pay insurance benefits of RMB 1,140 to the plaintiff Fang Zebo, the beneficiary designated by Fang Fengrong; payment shall be made within ten days after the judgment takes effect.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the defendant appealed to the Shantou Intermediate People's Court, on the same grounds as in the original trial.

The Shantou Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, held that the simplified personal insurance contract entered into between the appellant and the appellee's father, Fang Fengrong, clearly stated that persons suffering from cancer and other diseases were not eligible to apply for insurance. Fang Fengrong had already suffered from cancer before applying for insurance. Although he underwent surgical treatment, it did not result in a complete cure, and his condition soon worsened, leading to death. Fang Fengrong's health condition did not meet the insurance conditions. Since Fang Fengrong concealed his illness when applying for personal insurance, in accordance with Article 7 of the Simplified Personal Insurance Regulations, which provides that if the insured or the applicant conceals or deceives regarding the insurance conditions, the insurance company shall not pay insurance benefits, his civil act was invalid. Pursuant to Article 61(1) of the General Principles of the Civil Law, after the civil act of the appellee's father, Fang Fengrong, is confirmed as invalid, the insurance company shall not be liable for paying insurance benefits upon Fang Fengrong's death, but shall refund the insurance premiums paid by the applicant. The appellee's claim that the appellant should pay insurance benefits lacked sufficient grounds and was not sustained. The first-instance court's judgment that the insurance contract entered into between the appellant and the appellee's father, Fang Fengrong, was valid involved an improper application of law and should be corrected.

Accordingly, on November 17, 1989, the Shantou Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 151(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), rendered the following judgment:

1. The first-instance judgment of the Huilai County People's Court in this case is reversed.

2. The appellant, Huilai County Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China, shall pay the appellee, Fang Zebo, a surrender value of RMB 60, to be paid in a lump sum within ten days after the judgment takes effect.
